ClaimText: - CON-001 — The metric's **input-selection rule is the open surface itself**. `PRD.md` §11 metric 5 counts one population — parity DriftFindings — while `PRD.md` §7.1 defines one entity type serving two comparisons with two different producers (CLM-007, CLM-008). Each producer's accepted contract binds only its own side: the parity producer's obliges every finding it emits to carry its comparison identity, and the snapshot-drift producer's obliges its findings never to be "presented, exported, or counted as practitioner-harness parity output", while both expressly decline to fix a discriminating field on the shared type, which is the schema owner's question (CLM-013, CLM-014). No accepted source states how *this* consumer — which is not either producer — identifies a parity finding within the shared population. This contract therefore does not invent a discriminator: REQ-002 obliges the inclusion rule to be declared against whatever identity the accepted upstream contracts actually oblige, and REQ-006 obliges a count that cannot be made on that basis to be reported as a coverage limitation rather than as a figure. Adding a field, proposing a schema change, or selecting on an undocumented convention would settle an upstream schema question in the wrong deliverable.
AcceptedSourceRefs: PRD v2.2; SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md rev1.3; accepted upstream contracts
Notes: No semantic repair identified against the accepted basis.

ClaimText: - CON-002 — The **denominator is undefined between two accepted reconcile forms**. `SOW-093` and `PRD.md` §11 metric 5 both say "per reconcile" unqualified, while the accepted corpus defines two reconcile acts — the one-command full rebuild (`PEC-RCN-001`, `SOW-010`) and the Git-delta incremental run (`PEC-RCN-003`, `SOW-018`) — and attributes drift classification to "the reconciler" without distinguishing them (CLM-009). The question intersects an upstream open record: the parity producer's contract records that the *trigger* of a parity run is fixed by no accepted source and that "per reconcile" fixes the relation between a run and a reconcile but not the mechanism (CLM-014). Whether the denominator counts full rebuilds, incremental runs, or both changes what the metric means — a full-rebuild-only denominator and an all-reconciles denominator are different rates over the same numerator. This contract does not choose: REQ-002 obliges the denominator to be declared and REQ-013 obliges any operational reading adopted to produce a figure to be marked as unsettled rather than as accepted definition.

ClaimText: - CON-003 — No accepted source states a **threshold, target, direction, or interpretation rule** for metric 5. `PRD.md` §11 item 5 is a bare measurement statement (CLM-002); the §11 falsification clause names harness poll adoption and owner dashboard consultation as its two conditions and the ledger annotates those two limbs against other deliverables, with no limb annotation on `SOW-093` (CLM-003). ClaimText: - AX-001 — `OBJ-006` governs: "The product thesis remains measurable and falsifiable: adoption, parity, defect, and collision metrics are gathered in system behavior and the §11 falsification clause stays armed", `SourceRef` `§11`, with mapped scope items "SOW-020, SOW-057..060, SOW-064, SOW-084, SOW-085, SOW-093" and `MappedDeliverables` "DEL-01-04, DEL-03-04, DEL-10-01, DEL-10-04, DEL-10-05, DEL-10-09, DEL-10-10, DEL-10-11, DEL-10-12" (`SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md` §3 objectives table). Parity is one of the four named metric families, and this deliverable is the one that gathers it. A metric that could not report a bad number would make the thesis unfalsifiable in exactly the dimension it exists to measure, which is why REQ-006 forbids a comfortable figure over an incomplete derivation and REQ-001 forbids an imputed one.

The `PKG-10` charter states the same at package level by putting "The behaviors under test (their home packages)" out of scope (CLM-006). A metric deliverable that reached across that line — deriving its own comparison because the input was inconvenient, or asking the producer for a field — would collapse a measured system into its own measurement.

The metric is stated per reconcile because the measured behaviour recurs, not because this deliverable is a standing obligation — and the two are kept apart deliberately, because writing this contract as a standing assertion would claim a classification the exhibit does not give it, while writing its figures as one-shot would misdescribe what it counts. Where the absence of one blocks a figure, the answer is a stated limitation (REQ-006) and an owner question (AC-014, AC-015), not an obligation invented downstream.
